title: Haitian Creole 2: Everyday Grammar & Sentence Building
subtitle: Extend your foundations into more precise everyday Kreyòl.
description: An A1 continuation of Haitian Creole Foundations that adds article selection, contracted pronouns, deeper possession, expanded questions, health language, past and future time, and natural descriptions without reteaching Course 1.

courseOverview.recommendedSequence: Complete the modules in order. Course 1 language is assumed and reused only as context; each topic should add a genuinely new communicative pattern.
courseOverview.summary: Begin with singular definite article selection, then extend pronouns and possession, add new questions and health language, move familiar actions into past and future, and finish with natural descriptions.

moduleSummary.title: Choose the Right Definite Article
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Extend the noun-phrase foundation from Course 1 by using the noun's ending sound to choose the singular definite article.

moduleSummary.title: Short Pronouns & Deeper Possession
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Make sentences more natural with contracted object pronouns and standalone singular and plural possessive pronouns.

moduleSummary.title: More Questions & Health
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Add genuinely new question words and give them an immediate everyday use in simple health exchanges.

moduleSummary.title: Talk About Past & Future
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Let learners place familiar actions in yesterday, now, and tomorrow without reteaching present progressive.

moduleSummary.title: Describe People & Things Naturally
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Move from simple identity statements to natural descriptions of states, people, places, and things.

authoringGuidance: This course must use subjectSlug haitian-creole, courseSlug haitian-creole-everyday-grammar, catalogSlug haitian-creole, and profileId language.
English is the current source/instruction locale; the language being learned is Kreyòl Ayisyen.
Course 1 is a prerequisite. Reuse its language naturally but do not create lessons whose primary purpose is to reteach Course 1 content.
Do not force four topics per module. This course currently uses three or four only where the source material needs them.
Do not force every exercise kind into every topic. Select the skill activity that fits the language being introduced.
Use official Kreyòl orthography and preserve meaningful diacritics and apostrophes as supported by the supplied source material.
voice_input is transcript-based speaking practice. Do not claim phoneme-level pronunciation scoring.
Use locale ht-HT for authored speech/listening activities unless a specific provider requires the ht fallback.
Do not use code_input or pseudocode_input anywhere in this course.
Do not silently reconcile contradictory examples in the supplied documents. Avoid grading the disputed form until it is intentionally resolved.
The Week 2 source gives both plim nan and plim lan; Course 2 must not grade plim article selection unless that contradiction is explicitly resolved later.
Module 1 is free; later modules inherit the paid course access policy.

assessmentAndDelivery.suggestedBeginnerRhythm: Complete a topic when the learner can use its new pattern in context; do not add review topics merely to satisfy a fixed count.
recommendedCourseDeliverables: Functional question, health, time, and description exchanges
toolingSuggestions: Audio playback with Kreyòl speech locale support
Speech transcription with ht/ht-HT support when available
Text and word-bank practice in the learner workspace

modules.title: Choose the Right Definite Article
modules.description: Move beyond knowing that the definite article follows the noun and learn to choose among a, la, an, lan, and nan.
modules.purpose: Extend the noun-phrase foundation from Course 1 by using the noun's ending sound to choose the singular definite article.
learningObjectives: Choose a or la in source-supported noun phrases.
Choose an, lan, or nan in source-supported noun phrases.
Use article selection while listening, speaking, building, and writing familiar noun phrases.
guidedExercises: Compare a small number of source-supported examples before practicing a new example.
Use listening when the noun ending is the important cue.
Use building or writing only after the article-selection pattern has been introduced.

sections.title: Article Selection
sections.description: Choose the singular definite article from the ending sound of the noun.

topics.title: Choose a or la
topics.summary: Use the Week 2 sound patterns to distinguish a from la.
learningGoals: Recognize source-supported noun endings that take a.
Recognize source-supported noun endings that take la.
Apply the distinction to new examples from the Week 2 practice list.

topics.title: Choose an, lan, or nan
topics.summary: Use Week 2 ending patterns to distinguish the three nasal article forms.
learningGoals: Use an with the source-supported nasal-ending patterns.
Use lan with the source-supported nasal-plus-consonant and uncommon iy/uit patterns.
Use nan with the source-supported m, nn, èn, and òn endings.

topics.title: Hear and Use Definite Articles
topics.summary: Choose among all five singular article forms in mixed listening and production practice.
learningGoals: Listen for the noun ending before selecting the article.
Build and say complete noun phrases with the appropriate article.
Write source-supported noun phrases without relying on an English article pattern.

modules.title: Short Pronouns & Deeper Possession
modules.description: Extend known pronouns into short object forms and deeper possessive-pronoun patterns without reteaching Course 1 ownership or demonstratives.
modules.purpose: Build on Course 1 pronoun and possession knowledge with contracted object pronouns and standalone possessive pronouns from the Week 3 source.
learningObjectives: Use m, w, l, and n in source-supported object positions.
Recognize source-supported singular and plural possessive pronouns.
Distinguish object-pronoun forms from possessive-pronoun forms without reteaching known Course 1 possession patterns.
guidedExercises: Reuse Course 1 pronouns and noun phrases as known material.
Introduce only the new contracted or possessive pattern needed for the task.
Practice the new form in short complete sentences.
quizFocus: contracted object pronouns m, w, l, n
yo without a contracted object form

sections.title: Pronouns and Possession
sections.description: Extend known pronouns and possession into shorter, more flexible sentence patterns.

topics.title: Use Short Object Pronouns
topics.summary: Use m, w, l, and n in source-supported object positions.
learningGoals: Connect full pronouns with their contracted object forms.
Recognize the object pronoun in a short sentence.
Produce short source-supported sentences with contracted objects.

topics.title: Use Possessive Pronouns
topics.summary: Distinguish mine, yours, his or hers, ours, and theirs using the Week 3 patterns.
learningGoals: Recognize singular possessive-pronoun forms.
Recognize plural possessive-pronoun forms.
Use a possessive pronoun in a short contrast.

modules.title: More Questions & Health
modules.description: Extend the Course 1 question toolkit and use it with body and health language.
modules.purpose: Add genuinely new question words and give them an immediate everyday use in simple health exchanges.
learningObjectives: Use new Week 4 question forms without reteaching the Course 1 core question set.
Recognize common body-part vocabulary from the source.
Say what hurts using the source's fèmal expressions.
guidedExercises: Treat Course 1 question structures as known.
Introduce only the new question word needed for each exchange.
Use body vocabulary in short functional questions and answers.

sections.title: Questions and Health
sections.description: Ask for more specific information and use the questions in a simple health context.

topics.title: Ask for More Specific Information
topics.summary: Add Week 4 question forms that were not explicitly taught in Course 1.
learningGoals: Recognize the new question forms from the Week 4 source.
Choose the question word that fits the information being requested.
Produce short questions without reteaching known Course 1 forms.

topics.title: Name Body Parts
topics.summary: Learn only the body vocabulary needed for the health expressions in the source.
learningGoals: Recognize common body-part words from Week 4.
Match heard body-part words to written Kreyòl.
Use selected body-part words in short phrases.

topics.title: Say What Hurts
topics.summary: Use fèmal expressions for common aches from the Week 4 source.
learningGoals: Recognize common fèmal expressions.
Say which body part hurts.
Use a short health question-and-answer exchange.

modules.title: Talk About Past & Future
modules.description: Add te and pral while treating simple present and ap as known Course 1 language.
modules.purpose: Let learners place familiar actions in yesterday, now, and tomorrow without reteaching present progressive.
learningObjectives: Use te before a verb for source-supported past actions.
Use pral before a verb for source-supported future actions.
Contrast past, known present patterns, and future in short everyday statements.
guidedExercises: Start from action sentences the learner already knows.
Change only the time marker or time expression needed for the new meaning.
Use timeline contrasts rather than abstract tense terminology where possible.

sections.title: Past and Future
sections.description: Move familiar actions backward and forward in time.

topics.title: Use te for Past Actions
topics.summary: Place te before a familiar verb to talk about a completed past action.
learningGoals: Recognize te before a verb.
Build a short past statement.
Connect a past-time word such as yè with a te statement.

topics.title: Use pral for Future Actions
topics.summary: Place pral before a familiar verb to talk about a future action.
learningGoals: Recognize pral before a verb.
Build a short future statement.
Connect demen with a pral statement.

topics.title: Contrast Yesterday, Today & Tomorrow
topics.summary: Choose between te, known present patterns, and pral in short contexts.
learningGoals: Identify whether an action is past, present, or future from context.
Choose te or pral only when the time meaning requires it.
Produce a short three-time contrast using familiar verbs.

modules.title: Describe People & Things Naturally
modules.description: Use Week 7 description patterns, ye, and adjectives while treating basic identity se as known.
modules.purpose: Move from simple identity statements to natural descriptions of states, people, places, and things.
learningObjectives: Recognize descriptions where English to be is not expressed in Kreyòl.
Use ye in source-supported questions and closing statements.
Use adjectives in source-supported noun phrases and descriptions.
Use selected colors, sizes, and qualities in everyday descriptions.
guidedExercises: Do not reteach basic se identity from Course 1.
Contrast known identity language with the new Week 7 description patterns.
Introduce adjective vocabulary only as needed for a meaningful description.
quizFocus: descriptions without an expressed to be

sections.title: Descriptions
sections.description: Describe states and things with the Week 7 patterns.

topics.title: Describe Without an Expressed to be
topics.summary: Use source-supported state and description sentences where English uses is or are but Kreyòl does not.
learningGoals: Recognize state descriptions without se.
Build short descriptions of people and things.
Avoid inserting se into source patterns where it is not used.

topics.title: Use ye
topics.summary: Use ye in the Week 7 question and statement patterns.
learningGoals: Recognize ye at the end of source-supported questions.
Use ye in short questions about people, things, or location.
Recognize a short closing statement with ye.

topics.title: Place Adjectives in Phrases
topics.summary: Notice and use adjective placement in the Week 7 examples.
learningGoals: Locate the describing word in a source-supported noun phrase.
Build a short noun phrase with an adjective.
Read a description without translating word by word from English.

topics.title: Describe Color, Size & Quality
topics.summary: Use a practical subset of the Week 7 adjective lists in complete descriptions.
learningGoals: Use selected color words in descriptions.
Use selected size words in descriptions.
Use selected quality words in descriptions without memorizing the full source table at once.
